races.name: Blackmore Building Contractors Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Em Four
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Jamie Osborne, Saffie riding, but recent form is patchy (785 last three) and the sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 comparable runs suggests she needs everything to go right at the rear.|

runners_data.name: Nogo's Dream
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners this 6-year-old hold-up type who has solid going-form (1W4P in 10 similar ground runs) and a second at this course-and-distance combination; drops off the pace naturally but needs the front to collapse.|

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a tongue-tie/visor combination for Stuart Williams; won 5f on good ground 16 days ago and the 7lb claimer Olivia Haines keeps weight low — well-placed to track Kento and strike.|

runners_data.name: South Shore
runners_data.note: In terrific recent form (1122) with two wins on similar going, but his natural instinct is to close from the rear; squeezed into midfield by the field's configuration, his STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence that he will reproduce that closing burst from this position.|

runners_data.name: Secret Handsheikh
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who has won twice in his last six on comparable going, including a 6f win on good; prominent style suits tracking Kento, the visor is retained, and Joe Leavy's positive ride could see him delivered at the ideal moment.|

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed leader for Tony Carroll, drawn to control this race from the outset; his sim-going record is modest (1W5P from 6) but uncontested fractions on fast ground at Brighton play to his strengths, and Ray Dawson can dictate the fractions.|

races.paceDynamic: Kento is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival capable of matching his early pace, he should stride into an uncontested lead from the gates on this good-to-firm Brighton 5½f. Secret Handsheikh and Merrimack will press from prominent positions, giving the race a measured but honest gallop that neither dawdles nor collapses. South Shore is a genuine hold-up horse who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more hold-up types than the rear positions can accommodate — Em Four and Nogo's Dream are the truest closers and will be last or near last, leaving South Shore racing somewhat out of natural role. This shape — a lone leader setting a controlled, uncontested tempo — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just behind Kento and pounce, giving Secret Handsheikh and Merrimack the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kento Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Kento secures the lead unchallenged and Secret Handsheikh or Merrimack track him in an honest rhythm before striking.
scenarios.body: Kento sets a sustainable pace on good-to-firm going and the prominent duo, travelling within his slipstream, have enough petrol to accelerate through the final furlong before the closers arrive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Overhaul Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kento sets a genuinely fast early clip that burns out the prominent horses, leaving a vacuum for true hold-up types to fill.
scenarios.body: Nogo's Dream and Em Four, dropped out from the start, suddenly find daylight on the outside as the pace collapses in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: South Shore Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If South Shore, despite racing out of his deepest hold-up role, finds a clear run from midfield and times his run better than the prominent horses.
scenarios.body: His recent wins from 5f and strong going form give him raw ability to compensate for a sub-optimal position, and if the prominent horses check each other he can slice through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds All
scenarios.trigger: If Kento, given a completely soft lead at a measured pace, simply is never headed and the small field fails to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: A field of six on a tight Brighton sprint can produce a blanket finish, but if the closers misjudge their move and the prominent pair are flat, Kento's fitness on 19 days off could be enough to steal.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Secret Handsheikh or Merrimack attempt to press Kento hard early — if either goes for the lead at the break, the pace dynamic shifts and closers Em Four and Nogo's Dream become significantly more dangerous.
South Shore's redistribution to midfield means he may get shuffled wide on Brighton's curved track when trying to find a run — monitor his draw and early positioning relative to Merrimack.

Nogo's Dream's jockey Billy Loughnane must judge the pace precisely from the rear in a small six-runner field; in a compressed finish on 5½f there is limited room to make up ground if he is more than two lengths off the pace at halfway.
Kento has run 19 days since his last start — watch paddock freshness and early gate behaviour; if he misses the break the entire pace shape unravels and the race becomes genuinely open.

races.name: Cognitive Law EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.note: Hannon-trained hold-up type with a form string of 77604 that reflects consistent moderate efforts, though three placings from five starts are absent — true style is rear-tracking, nudged to midfield in the map only because the rear is over-subscribed; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers its chance in a shape where hold-up horses struggle to land a blow on fast Brighton ground.

runners_data.name: I Am Royal
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes debutant for Billy Loughnane carrying top weight; entirely unexposed so style and ceiling are unknown, but Hughes has four winners from 29 runners over 14 days and Loughnane's forward-riding instinct could see this horse race prominently from the gates.

runners_data.name: Major Looktwice
runners_data.note: Third on debut over 6f on Good ground at similar going to today, giving it the best form reference among the unexposed runners; Gary & Josh Moore partnership send it out 14 days later, and Tom Queally is likely to place it prominently given that prior closing effort.

runners_data.name: Rogue Imperial
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed leader, four runs at 6f on Good ground with two placings — this horse knows its job and Archie Watson's absence from the winners' column over 14 days adds no pressure; the key question is whether a controlled solo lead on fast ground is enough to hold on.

runners_data.name: Roll Up Raymond
runners_data.note: Gihan Arnolda's sole runner in the period, a once-raced hold-up type who finished third over 6f on Good ground — Ray Dawson rides and the horse's natural inclination to come from behind makes it reliant on others setting a strong enough pace, which is not guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Happy Daisy
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams sends out this hold-up filly 24 days after a modest seventh of 6f on Good ground; Marco Ghiani will look to settle her, but the combination of a weak closing profile, a course that doesn't reward late runners, and the lowest recorded finishing position in the field makes her the hardest to back.

races.paceDynamic: Rogue Imperial is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and should lead from the gates unchallenged, setting a sustainable and controlled tempo over Brighton's 6f undulating straight. With no genuine rival willing or able to dispute the lead, Rogue Imperial can dictate from the front without burning excessive early energy, making this a leader-friendly shape. From Me To You, Roll Up Raymond, and Happy Daisy are all natural hold-up types, though the field's pace architecture means From Me To You has been redistributed to a midfield mapping — in reality the rear-group cluster is larger than the race shape can neatly show. The race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can travel in the slipstream of Rogue Imperial and pounce before the hold-up horses can generate momentum from further back on this relatively short, flat track where sustained closing runs are harder to deliver.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Imperial dictates a comfortable gallop and the hold-up horses fail to generate a meaningful late challenge.
scenarios.body: Rogue Imperial goes unchallenged to the lead and sets fractions that suit his stamina at 6f on Good to Firm ground, where he has placed twice; with no pressure horse to wind up the pace, the leader may simply never get headed. Prominent types like Major Looktwice and I Am Royal, racing close to the pace on debut or near-debut, are best placed to capitalise if the leader flattens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominently-placed debutant or lightly-raced runner tracks Rogue Imperial and finds the extra gear inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Major Looktwice or I Am Royal, both unraced or near-unraced, settle just off the lead and use fresh legs to accelerate past Rogue Imperial approaching the final furlong on the fast ground. The unexposed profile of both runners means a forward tactical ride from Loughnane or Queally could unlock significant improvement over the sole previous effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the hold-up horses find a clear run to close with purpose inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: From Me To You or Happy Daisy, with genuine hold-up profiles, close to within striking range if the front end over-commits slightly; however, Brighton's 6f straight rarely offers the sustained momentum phase that true closers need, limiting the ceiling on this scenario. The redistribution of From Me To You to midfield further dilutes the group's collective closing punch.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic, No Clear Beneficiary
scenarios.trigger: If erratic early positioning from the debut runners causes interference or a pace collapse, scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: One or more of the unraced or once-raced runners breaks poorly or overreacts to early movement, fragmenting the orderly leader-prominent dynamic and creating a lottery finish. In this scenario the winner is likely whoever happens to be best positioned mid-race, with Roll Up Raymond's prior form at the trip and going offering a marginal edge.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rogue Imperial's early splits — if Harry Davies allows him to coast at a very relaxed pace, the lead margin entering the final furlong could be too large for any hold-up horse to overcome on this tight Brighton 6f.

I Am Royal and Major Looktwice are completely or near-completely unexposed — either could show unexpected early speed or greenness that disrupts the anticipated running order; monitor their pre-race behaviour and loading.

From Me To You carries a STYLE_FIT discount and is mapped out of its natural hold-up role; if it fails to find clear daylight in the last two furlongs after racing in midfield, its chances will evaporate quickly on this shorter track.

Brighton 6f Good to Firm conditions today are confirmed by the going report — fast ground suits forward-going horses and reduces the closing window, reinforcing the leader-prominent bias across all scenarios.

Roll Up Raymond's trainer Gihan Arnolda has only three runners in the 14-day window — a small, selective operation; monitor market moves for late support that might signal stable confidence not reflected in the form.

races.name: Ian Carnaby Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Von Krolock
runners_data.note: Won two of his last six and has placed at Brighton over this trip in Good ground before; Christian Howarth's 3lb claim helps at the weights and the horse's prominent style suits this pace map perfectly, though only 2 from 15 on similar going tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Nordic Glory
runners_data.note: Landed his last win over 6f on Firm and has a fair record on Good-to-Firm ground; Owen Lewis's 5lb claim is meaningful, but 10 of 15 similar-going runs have yielded no wins or places at this level and the 24-day gap needs monitoring.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with the best similar-going strike rate in this field (9 from 15), one win and two places, and she wears a hood; her 12-day turnaround is acceptable and she is the one runner whose natural style aligns with a late-closing scenario without redistribution caveats.

runners_data.name: Rye
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, but a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) suggests she is not ideally placed in this race shape and a long 80-day break is a notable concern; Marco Ghiani will need to judge the fractions precisely to avoid setting it up for trackers behind her.

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and Billy Loughnane takes over for Gerard O'Leary after a 55-day break; a hold-up operator whose recent form reads poorly (double-figure finishes in Good ground), and Good To Firm on a flat course does not obviously change that profile.

runners_data.name: The Organiser
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave partners this 7yo who has genuine hold-up tendencies but has been mapped to midfield because the rear is crowded; his last five runs have all been over 7f and stepping back to 6f on Good To Firm is an unexplored combination — the style-fit discount is real here.

runners_data.name: Be An Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly has won and placed on Good ground over this trip and the blinkers are a positive trigger; genuinely a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot by the race shape, so her ability to deliver her effort depends heavily on how the pace plays out ahead of her.

runners_data.name: Unico
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon's 5yo wears a hood and has been off 76 days, a layoff that warrants caution; a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield in the map, and with only 3 from 15 on similar going and no wins, the style-fit penalty is warranted — finishing position will depend on whether the race falls apart late.

races.paceDynamic: Rye is the one confirmed front-runner here and on Good To Firm ground over Brighton's 6f she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested tempo — no significant pressure is expected to come from behind to force a pace collapse. Von Krolock and Nordic Glory are genuine prominent types who will look to track Rye closely, creating a compact early order where the first three positions are effectively settled before the field straightens. The race shape is therefore one of moderate, controlled pace with a small group going clear of the trailing cluster — this strongly favours runners who can travel prominently and kick off a steady gallop rather than those forced to close from well off the pace. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can honestly place at the rear; The Organiser, Be An Angel, and Unico are all true closers redistributed into midfield on the map, but in this actual race shape they will likely find themselves unable to fully close the gap Rye's group opens up — prominence is the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rye Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Rye leads unmolested at a steady clip and the prominent trackers Von Krolock and Nordic Glory time their runs to perfection.
scenarios.body: Rye sets a fair gallop on Good To Firm ground and those tucked in just behind can switch off before producing their effort in the final two furlongs; on Brighton's undulating surface the prominent group will have enough in reserve to hold off any late challenges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Rye's pace drops away in the final furlong and one of the tracking prominent types accelerates through to win.
scenarios.body: Von Krolock or Nordic Glory, travelling smoothly just off Rye's shoulder, produces a decisive kick once the leader flattens; the steady early gallop means they have not been emptied out and can sustain their run to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Make Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to soften up the leaders and the trailing group can make meaningful late headway.
scenarios.body: Dark Sun, the sole true hold-up type properly placed at the rear, would be the primary beneficiary as she closes into a tiring field over the final furlong; Be An Angel, though redistributed from her natural role, could also benefit if she settles kindly and gets a clear passage late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Rye cuts out minimal fractions and the race crawls, causing a bunched finish where position becomes irrelevant.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race compresses the field and turns the contest into a sprint from the two-furlong pole, where superior finishing speed and freshness can trump tactical position; Blue Anthem, returning from 55 days off, and Dark Sun with her solid Good ground record could emerge from the pack if the pace is truly dawdling.

watchPoints.text: Rye's 80-day absence combined with her STYLE_FIT flag means she could either set a flat, slow gallop or fade sharply in the final furlong — monitor her early jumping and how easily she finds her stride.

Von Krolock and Nordic Glory are both prominent types likely to press Rye closely; if both commit early, a minor pace duel could develop between the three leaders which would accelerate the tempo and shift the balance toward closers Dark Sun and Be An Angel.

Dark Sun is the only genuine hold-up horse properly positioned at the rear and her similar-going record (1W 2P from 9) stands out — if this race is run at any pace at all she is the one horse capable of delivering a true late run without the redistribution caveat hanging over her.

The Organiser, Be An Angel, and Unico are all true closers who will in reality be running further back than the map shows; watch for traffic problems in the final two furlongs as three horses attempt to find space from similar positions behind a compact front group.

Blue Anthem's tongue-tie and 55-day break for a trainer with a 1-from-7 14-day record suggests he may need the run — monitor market moves in the hour before post time as a significant drift could confirm stable intentions.

races.name: Ian Carnaby 30 Years Of Sponsorship Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Jim & Suzi Best with George Wood up; lightly raced at this trip but 2/10f on good last time is encouraging — needs a strong pace to get competitive from the rear and the controlled tempo here may blunt her chance.

runners_data.name: Bownder
runners_data.note: Prominent racer 48 days off the track for Jonathan Portman, now fitted with a claiming jockey allowance; ran well twice at 10f on good and is the likeliest horse to shadow Bobacious, which puts her in an ideal tactical position if her fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Crimson Road
runners_data.note: Two recent wins over 10f on good ground give William Carson's mount strong course-condition credentials; races from hold-up but those wins suggest she can produce a sustained late effort — trainer in form with one winner from ten over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and pace anchor for this race; three wins from five placed efforts on good going and a recent 10f success confirm he handles conditions and the trip, and an uncontested lead from stall draws is the defining tactical factor here.

runners_data.name: Star Mind
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on soft but his last two efforts on comparable good ground have been poor (16th, 8th); his true style is hold-up and he's pushed forward on the map only because the rear is saturated — at OR 64 his form makes him a major query.

runners_data.name: Bohemian Breeze
runners_data.note: Tom Queally takes over on a horse who has won twice in recent form over 10f on good ground; a genuinely strong hold-up performer whose natural style is compromised by the crowded rear in this field, but if the pace fires up he is among the most talented closers here.

runners_data.name: It's Life
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides the lowest-weighted runner in the field at OR 56; genuine hold-up type who won over 8f on good recently and placed over 10f — trip and going are not concerns, but racing out of his natural deep position in a controlled-pace race is a significant obstacle.

runners_data.name: Twilight Guest
runners_data.note: Kieran O'Neill partners the bottom-rated runner (OR 45) who has run consistently in mid-to-rear positions over 10-12f on good; recent form shows a string of fourth-to-seventh finishes and George Margarson's stable is without a win in the past six days, making improvement hard to justify.

races.paceDynamic: Bobacious is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on this flat Brighton mile-and-two. Good to Firm ground will keep the pace honest but not extreme, meaning the race is unlikely to turn into a thorough stamina test — instead, a steady-to-moderate tempo from Bobacious sets up a race where the ability to travel prominently and quicken off the pace matters more than raw staying power. The field is deceptively hold-up heavy: Star Mind, Bohemian Breeze, It's Life, and Twilight Guest are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because genuine rear positions are overcrowded, while Bownder is the only runner likely to track Bobacious with any intent. Given a single, uncontested pace-setter and a clutch of hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal, this race shape strongly favours runners who can sit second or third, conserve energy on the rail, and produce a clean sustained run from two furlongs out — the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile has a clear structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bobacious Controls, Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious leads uncontested at a fair gallop and a prominent tracker lands a telling blow in the straight.
scenarios.body: Bobacious sets a comfortable pace with Bownder the most likely horse to shadow him, and the race resolves in the final two furlongs as those who tracked closest have the energy reserves to accelerate on fast ground; hold-up horses forced into midfield face a longer, less efficient run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bobacious Front-Runs, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled that Bobacious conserves enough to score from the front.
scenarios.body: A slow-to-moderate tempo allows Bobacious to bowl along unchallenged and simply never be headed, having done all his racing on his own terms; his recent win over 10f on good ground supports the trip and conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Overcome Disadvantage
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the hold-up types find enough daylight to deliver a late challenge.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop from Bobacious — perhaps pressed by an eager Bownder — burns off the prominent runners and opens the race up for those coming from off the pace; Bohemian Breeze and It's Life are the most capable hold-up performers if they can find a clear passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Outsider Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners tie each other up and both prominent and hold-up horses are delivered at the same time.
scenarios.body: A chaotic or contested pace sees multiple horses weakening simultaneously in the straight, gifting an unconsidered runner a winning opportunity; Star Mind's OR drop and Twilight Guest's course experience give them marginal claims in a scenario that is otherwise unlikely given the single dominant pace-setter.

watchPoints.text: Bobacious (front-runner) — if he is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged, the entire race shape resolves in his favour or that of his immediate tracker; watch whether Bownder's rider elects to press him or sit off.
Bownder's fitness after 48 days off — if she fades in the straight having tracked Bobacious, the door opens wide for the hold-up horses, fundamentally shifting which scenario unfolds.

Bohemian Breeze and It's Life are both natural hold-up horses forced closer than ideal; if they get boxed in or blocked by the compressed midfield group, their finishing kick could be wasted regardless of the pace shape.

Crimson Road's two recent 10f wins on good going make her the standout form pick in this field — watch whether William Carson elects to race prominently or play hold-up, as her position at the top of the straight will be the key visual cue.

Going is confirmed Good to Firm despite the race card listing Good — faster ground suits horses with clean, efficient actions and may stretch the hold-up types who need a stamina test to deliver their best.

races.name: Streamline Taxis Always Going The Distance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dalmally
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Mark Pattinson who has shown mid-division form over this trip and going, though sim-going figures (8 runs, no wins, 3 places) suggest consistency has been elusive; 32 days off and a claimer aboard are neutral factors, and the congested rear of this field presents a real traffic-management challenge.

runners_data.name: King David
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway's gelding carries a hood and races from well off the pace, but his Good to Firm record is thin (3 from 15 sim-going runs, no wins, no places) and recent form strings at Brighton-style sharp tracks have not encouraged; Saffie Osborne takes over but has limited material to work with here.

runners_data.name: Winemaker
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's yard has been in form (4/29 over 14 days) which is a live angle, and the headgear change (hood applied) could sharpen this hold-up type; however his sim-going record shows no wins in three relevant runs, and a wide-open mid-division berth means he must find clear daylight late.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Genuinely acts on Good to Firm ground and has winning form at this trip (1/8f/GOO), with Billy Loughnane a high-quality booking — but this horse is a true rear-runner that the map has pushed into a midfield slot it won't naturally occupy, meaning it must race somewhat against its instincts; the form (3rd last time out) is current and the going suits.

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: Birkett yard has been active and this mare has an outstanding sim-going profile (11/15, 3 wins, 4 places) — comfortably the best going record in the field — and recent placed efforts over this exact trip are compelling; like River Wharfe, she is a natural hold-up type displaced into midfield on the pace map by weight of numbers, though her class at this level makes her one of the most interesting runners.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Courage
runners_data.note: John Ryan's four-year-old has placed form over this trip in Good going (3rd and 4th in recent outings) and returns just six days after her last run, suggesting fitness is not a concern; a genuine hold-up racer who has been shown in midfield due to the overcrowded rear, her best chance depends on getting a clean run in a field that may bunch late.

runners_data.name: Sangara
runners_data.note: Sheena West's filly wears a hood and has placed at this trip on Good ground, but stepping back from 10f may not play to her strengths given her recent patterns; a true hold-up runner mapped into midfield, she has no winning form in sim-going conditions and a 19-day gap is unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Celtic John
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 42 days, and Pat Phelan's gelding has a modest sim-going record (3/15, no wins, no places); a natural deep closer that the map has shifted forward into a midfield position, his best hope is a strongly-run race that brings stamina into play, which this scenario is unlikely to deliver.

runners_data.name: Monks Mead
runners_data.note: The key pace-setter and the only horse in the race with a front-running profile, giving Nicola Currie the luxury of dictating terms uncontested; recent form shows four places from five runs on Good-adjacent going and a 9-day turnaround indicates trainer Mark Usher has her ready, though the STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is operating at the sharp end of her comfort zone against hold-up rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Monks Mead is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mile handicap on Good to Firm ground at Brighton, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Nicola Currie can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset without burning fuel fighting for position. Behind her, the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up horses — Dalmally, King David, Winemaker, River Wharfe, Heer's Sadie, Chloe's Courage, Sangara, and Celtic John all prefer to race off the pace — meaning the middle and rear of the race will be congested and positional battles will be fought out well behind the leader. Brighton's undulating mile is a track that rewards horses who can travel smoothly and pick up in the straight, but an uncontested leader on a sound surface sets the primary tactical puzzle for every hold-up horse in the field. This race shape strongly favours Monks Mead's profile if she can find a comfortable rhythm and deliver a sustained run in the straight, while closers must overcome both the disadvantage of a solo moderate pace and the traffic risk of a bunched field coming to challenge simultaneously. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — River Wharfe, Heer's Sadie, Chloe's Courage, and Sangara are all true hold-up horses mapped to midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy, with River Wharfe and Heer's Sadie — both showing recent form at this trip and going — the most likely to find competitive positions closest to the front of that chasing group.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Monks Mead Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead secures an uncontested lead and sets a controlled but honest gallop that tests the closers' stamina without inviting a sprint.
scenarios.body: Monks Mead dictates from the front on Good to Firm Brighton ground, her hold-up rivals unable to close the gap quickly enough through the undulating straight; a prominent racing position proves decisive when the field fails to coordinate a late challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Swamps Her
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Monks Mead is too slow and triggers a bunched, sprint-style finish that swamps the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race compresses the field approaching the home straight, creating a scramble finish where the hold-up horses who travel best — particularly those with strong Good to Firm form — surge past.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong-Staying Closer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead sets a genuinely testing pace that catches out the mid-division horses but leaves a gap for a deep closer with stamina.
scenarios.body: A horse who has been settled at the back and makes smooth late progress — rather than fighting for mid-race position — picks off tiring rivals in the last two furlongs on ground that rewards genuine staying power.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead fades sharply inside the final two furlongs having set too hot a pace, gifting the race to whoever travels most smoothly through the congestion.
scenarios.body: The mid-division horses who best handled the muddled pace dynamics inherit the race late; a horse that combines recent Good to Firm form with an ability to quicken from a handy position benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Monks Mead sets the pace entirely alone — watch whether Nicola Currie elects to bowl along or plays possum at a crawl, because the tempo she chooses will determine whether this is a race for the front-runner or a sprint finish for the closers.

Heer's Sadie has the standout going stats in the field (11/15 sim-going, 3 wins) and is a hold-up horse forced to operate closer to the pace than ideal — watch if Christian Howarth (3) can find a position that lets her travel without being hampered by the bunched mid-division.

River Wharfe won over 8f on Good ground last time and Billy Loughnane is a significant jockey upgrade — if he can negotiate the congested middle section and get a clear run into the straight, this horse's form makes it a live threat under the top jockey.

The field has eight hold-up horses behind one front-runner — watch for significant traffic issues on Brighton's tight home straight, where blocked runs could cost several runners any realistic chance regardless of their underlying ability.

Going reported as Good to Firm at 4:30 despite the race card listing Good — horses with confirmed Good to Firm form (Heer's Sadie, River Wharfe) gain a marginal edge over those whose sim-going data is thinner on this surface.

races.paceDynamic: Kondratiev Wave is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 7f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Brighton, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Billy Loughnane can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured. Girls Allowed is the only other runner with a prominent profile and may track closely, but she lacks the pace or profile to force a true test on Kondratiev Wave early. The field behind is stacked with hold-up types — Superstorm, Berning Hot, Thanks Dad, Nautical Sky, Neat And Tidy, Barry The Worm and Mister Sandman all prefer to race off the pace — meaning the closers will need late momentum, but an uncontested moderate gallop over 7f at Brighton may leave them with too much to do if the leader conserves energy. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profile: a lone pace-setter controlling a falsely-run race on fast ground is the dominant tactical advantage, and horses who can travel prominently without fighting their position are best placed. Several redistributed runners (Neat And Tidy, Barry The Worm, Mister Sandman, Nautical Sky) are true hold-up horses shown in midfield only because the map cannot accommodate the volume of closers at the rear — of the genuine hold-up brigade, Superstorm and Berning Hot are most likely to secure a forward pitch in running.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kondratiev Wave Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave leads without pressure and sets a controlled gallop that denies closers a true test.
scenarios.body: Loughnane settles Kondratiev Wave in front on easy terms, the moderate pace suits a horse who has shown front-running ability over this C&D trip, and the uphill finish at Brighton is covered before the hold-up pack can organise a meaningful challenge. On Good to Firm ground with no genuine pace rival, this shape rewards the horse in front who controls the race from the off.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and the two or three horses with the best finishing gears pick up early enough to catch Kondratiev Wave.
scenarios.body: Superstorm and Berning Hot, both capable of travelling prominently from hold-up positions, get a clean run through and find the final two furlongs coming to them as the leader begins to tie up. Good to Firm ground and a relatively short 7f trip at Brighton is at the limit of their natural hold-up game, but recent form and trainer confidence makes them credible challengers if timing is right.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop collapses in the final two furlongs and multiple hold-up horses arrive simultaneously from midfield.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race can sometimes over-stretch the leader in the closing stages of Brighton's undulating finish, allowing a wave of closers to arrive together and produce a surprising result. Thanks Dad — who won over 6f on Good recently — and Mister Sandman could benefit from any bunching, though both carry style-fit concerns from their redistributed positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Girls Allowed Challenges Prominently
scenarios.trigger: If Girls Allowed tracks Kondratiev Wave assertively and produces enough acceleration to overhaul the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Girls Allowed showed a place effort over 7f on Good and a prominent style suits this race shape; if she travels smoothly in second and Kondratiev Wave hits the rising ground hard, she could grab the prize. This is a lower-probability shape because it depends on the leader weakening, which is not guaranteed given the lack of early pressure.

watchPoints.text: Kondratiev Wave (Billy Loughnane) — watch whether it is allowed to stride on unchallenged from the start; if it gets the lead uncontested inside the first furlong, the race shape crystallises immediately in its favour.

Superstorm (Mikkel Mortensen) — watch its position leaving the stalls; if the visor has it alert and it travels smoothly in midfield rather than being held up, it becomes the most dangerous late challenger to the leader.

Girls Allowed (Dylan Hogan) — watch whether Hogan sends her forward assertively to track Kondratiev Wave; if she settles directly behind the leader, she becomes the most obvious threat to the front-runner in the straight.

Mister Sandman and Barry The Worm — both true hold-up horses compressed into midfield by the race map; if either is ridden closer than their natural style dictates, they could be caught wide around Brighton's turns and lose more ground than anticipated.

Thanks Dad (Kieran O'Neill) — the tongue-tie and visor combination is worth watching at the start; Brighton's undulating track has not suited it previously, and any sluggish break or wide draw issue would likely end its chances before the race truly begins.
